title: Execute husbandry processes according to industry standards

lessons.title: Grading, stocking and moving fish
lessons.html:
Why we grade fish

Fish in one tank do not all grow at the same speed. Big fish eat more and can bully or even eat small fish. Catfish are known for this. Grading means sorting fish into size groups. Each group then goes into its own tank. This gives even growth and less fighting.

How grading is done

  1. Stop feeding before grading, as your supervisor says.
  2. Lower the water or crowd the fish gently with a net.
  3. Use a grader. This is a box or frame with bars at a set gap. Small fish swim through. Big fish stay behind.
  4. Move each size group quickly into its new tank with clean, aerated water.
  5. Count or weigh a sample of each group and write it down.

Stocking density

Stocking density is how many fish (or how many kilograms of fish) are in a tank or pond. Too many fish use up oxygen and make the water dirty. Too few fish waste space. The manager sets the right number. Your job is to count carefully and stock the number on the plan.

Moving fish between tanks

  • Check the new tank is clean, full and has air running.
  • Check the temperature of both waters. If they are very different, let the fish adjust slowly. Float the bag or mix the waters a little at a time.
  • Carry fish in water, not dry.
  • Never overload a bucket or transport tank.

Transport on the bakkie

When fish travel in a tank on the bakkie, keep the air or oxygen running. Drive smoothly. Park in the shade. Check fish on the way on long trips. Keep the transport tank clean and disinfected between loads.

lessons.title: Doing the work to standard every day
lessons.html:
Working to standard

A standard is the agreed correct way to do a job. The farm writes its procedures in a book or on charts. Follow them every time, even when nobody is watching. This keeps the fish healthy and the product safe to eat.

Feeding to standard

  • Weigh the feed for each tank from the feeding chart.
  • Feed at set times.
  • Watch the fish eat and stop when they slow down.
  • Write down what was fed and any feed left over.

Water to standard

  • Take readings at the set times: temperature, oxygen and others your farm uses.
  • Write readings with the time.
  • If a reading is out of range, act as the procedure says and tell your supervisor.

Biosecurity

Biosecurity means keeping disease out and stopping it spreading.

  • Use the foot bath at the entrance.
  • Keep each unit's nets and buckets separate.
  • Put new fish in a quarantine tank first if the farm does this.
  • Report sick or strange-looking fish quickly.

Sick fish

Signs include fish rubbing on walls, white spots, red sores, frayed fins, swollen bellies or not eating. Do not treat fish yourself. Tell your supervisor. Treatments must be given only as the vet or manager instructs and as the product label says.

Your own safety

  • Wear boots with grip and gloves.
  • Keep electrical equipment dry. Report damaged cables.
  • Wear eye protection and gloves when using salt, lime or disinfectant.
  • Never work alone at deep ponds.

Key points

  • Grade fish so each tank has fish of similar size.
  • Stock the number of fish on the plan.
  • Let fish adjust slowly when water temperatures differ.
  • Follow written procedures every time.
  • Report sick fish; never treat them on your own.
